newsitem.title: MEXICO: Analysts warily hail Penoles buy.
newsitem.headline: Analysts warily hail Penoles buy.

text.p: The world's largest refined silver producer's first international venture was greeted with reserved cheer on Monday as analysts said they needed more details on the deal from Mexico's Industrias Penoles.
Penoles became the majority owner of Peru's state-owned La Oroya complex with a winning bid of $185 million, beating out competitors U.S. Doe Run Co. and Switzerland's Glencore International.
"No one knows how long it will take to turn this thing around or whether it will consolidate the complex or list it as a subsidiary," Valores Finamex analyst Chris Albi said.

Penoles is expected to clarify this week what participation it will hold in La Oroya's capital, whether it will increase its minimum 51 percent stake or join with a partner. The company could buy the site from the government completely for another $192.6 million, state miner Centromin said.
Possible candidates to join in the bid are losing bidder Glencore and Spain's Asturiana de Zinc, analysts said.
Analysts also clamored for more information about the company, such as its debt load and operating margins.
"It's difficult to evaluate the price with only sales information and the percentage of what the company is buying," Serfin Brokerage Mexico City analyst Hector Novoa said.
"Operating margins for the government were probably small, which could be why it was so cheap," BBV-Probursa Mexico City analyst Jose Buendia said.
Despite concerns, analysts said they were confident Penoles management could make the venture work.
"I think Penoles's expertise will be able to turn it around on an operational level," Albi said.
"I think overall it is a good deal for Penoles and provides added value to shareholders in the medium term," Santander Investment Mexico City analyst Sandra Morfin said.
The pricetag may dilute profits in the short term, she said. The next highest bid for La Oroya was $121 million. The Peruvian government had set a minimum bid of $70 million.

The Oroya complex will account for Penoles's first revenues outside of Mexico and culminates months of struggling for the site. Penoles will be able to begin operations at the Peru complex by June 30.
With the new complex of smelters and refineries, Penoles solidifies a trend toward bolstering its refining activity over its mining interests, analysts said.
It also boosts the company's silver, zinc, lead, gold and copper output, and fires up competition with fellow miner and copper giant Grupo Mexico.
